title: Mini experiments log — quant & eval quicknotes
content:
Daily mini-log for iterative experiments; messy, ephemeral — meant for quick capture.

2026-02-18 \u2014 initial notes
- Goal: reduce cost/latency on 13B-ish workload for chat summarization while keeping answer quality > baseline (redwood-open-13b fp16).
- Baseline: redwood-open-13b fp16 on A100: 8.5 ms/token (measured avg), 0.72 ROUGE-L (eval set A, 512 context).

Quick experimental matrix (high level):
- EXP-Q001: GPTQ 8-bit, per-channel, group_size=128, clamp=0.0
  - env: docker:redwood/serve:qa-2026-02, python 3.11, vram target ~40GB
  - micro-batch=1, kv-cache warmup ON
  - rough perf: 13.7 ms/token on A100 (tokens/sec down ~40%)
  - eval: ROUGE-L 0.69, occasional hallucination on named entities
  - notes: calibration with 2k lines of dialogue seems insufficient; try 10k sample calibration

- EXP-Q002: 4-bit GPTQ (nf4-like), group_size=64, use act-order fallback
  - perf: 9.3 ms/token (promising), peak vram ~22GB
  - eval: ROUGE-L 0.66, but top-k sampling has higher repetition; try top-p 0.95 instead of 0.9
  - anomalies: beam search outputs diverge for long contexts (>1024)

- EXP-Q003: int8 symmetric, per-tensor, no calibration (fast conversion)
  - perf: 7.9 ms/token (faster than fp16 in some runs, likely due to better kernel path)
  - eval: ROUGE-L 0.63 (quality loss), but latency/cost win for non-critical paths

Prompt/eval snippets to reproduce:
- Prompt template A (summarization):
  """
  System: You are a concise summarizer.
  User: Summarize the following conversation in 3 bullets.
  Conversation:
  {{dialogue}}
  """
- Evaluation metric: ROUGE-L on curated eval set (n=300), plus human spot-check for named entities.

Calibration notes:
- Calibration dataset size matters: 2k -> noisy; 10k+ examples -> more stable quant scales. Use 10k samples sampled from production dialogues (short/medium/long).
- Try per-channel scale with outlier clipping at 99.9th percentile to avoid huge scale factors.

Operational checks (quick):
- Memory leak? watch docker container for 30min with continuous stream load (micro-batch 1 -> 2000 requests)
- KV-cache flush works after model rollover? observed stale tokens in EXP-Q002 run; probable bug in cache invalidation in runtime v0.9.7-qa

Things to try next (actionable TODOs):
1) Re-run EXP-Q002 with top-p=0.95 and temperature=0.6; measure repetition score (n-gram overlap metric).
2) EXP-Q001: increase calibration set to 12k, add per-channel outlier clipping at 99.9. Track scale hist distribution.
3) Investigate kernel fallback path that gave EXP-Q003 a surprising speedup vs fp16; add microbenchmark for GEMM paths (seq_len=512, 1024).
4) Add small human eval (5 raters, 30 samples) for named-entity hallucination check across Q001/Q002/Q003.
5) Create short reproducibility script: scripts/mini-quant-repro.sh (container + model + seed + evalset sha).

Observations and hypotheses:
- Hypothesis: 4-bit NF4-ish quantization with careful group_size and calibration gives most attractive latency/cost tradeoff but needs additional sampling tweaks to recover quality.
- Hypothesis: some 8-bit per-channel runs are stable quality-wise but kernel paths are not yet optimized (older CUDA kernels fall back to slower loops).

Quick wins for demo:
- Use EXP-Q002 (4-bit) with short contexts (<=512) and tuned sampling (top-p 0.95) for a cost-demo flow; highlight 30-40% cost reduction vs fp16 with small human eval showing \"negligible quality regression\".

Open questions (to resolve):
- Which calibration distribution matters more: token frequency tail vs typical production tokens? need ablation.
- Is group_size 64 always better than 128 for our models, or does it depend on layer shapes? run per-layer diagnostics.
- Should we prefer symmetric int8 for certain layers (FFN) and NF4 for attention? hybrid strategies to test.

Logs / quick command snippets:
- convert command (prototype): python quant/convert.py --model redwood-open-13b --out q/13b-q4-gs64 --mode gptq --group-size 64 --calib-file /mnt/calib/10k.json
- run eval: python eval/eval_summarize.py --model q/13b-q4-gs64 --evalset evalsets/summ-300.json --metrics rouge,lm-score --batch 2

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc as ephemeral; when stable, move summary to confluence and add reproducibility artifacts to GH.
- Ping Owen on kernel fallback issue (slack @owen) and Leah for human eval logistics.

2026-03-09 \u2014 follow-up entries
- Ran EXP-Q002 with top-p 0.95, temp=0.6: repetition reduced by 18% (ngram overlap), ROUGE-L stable at 0.67 (up from 0.66). Latency unchanged.
- EXP-Q001 with 12k calib: ROUGE-L improved to 0.70 (close to baseline) but latency still 12.9 ms/token. Memory footprint ok.

Next-sprint plan (very small):
- Priority A: EXP-Q002 sampling sweep + small human eval (owner: Nina, collaborator: Leah)
- Priority B: kernel microbench and open issue for runtime (owner: Owen)
- Backlog: hybrid quant per-layer experiments and per-layer scale diagnostics

End of scratch notes.
